findings.excerpt: The source explicitly defines the displayed commutative relation $\mathcal I_\Phi\circ q=S\circ T_\Phi$ and provides a tikzcd square.

findings.mathematical_check: The intended square has top arrow $T_\Phi:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^{[m]}$, left quotient map $q:\mathbb R^d\to Q_d$, right coordinatewise squaring $S$, and bottom intensity map $\mathcal I_\Phi:Q_d\to[0,\infty)^m$. These labels match the preceding definitions and identity. The diagram is explanatory; the source says no proof relies on it.

editorial_candidates.rationale: The definition is a geometric transform over a maximal nontangential geodesic and distinguishes the incoming and outgoing boundary behavior; a small schematic could make those roles immediate.
editorial_candidates.labels_maps_relations_to_draw_or_check: Draw a manifold domain with smooth boundary, one unit-speed interior geodesic arc γ:[0,L], an inward-pointing initial velocity at γ(0)∈∂M₀, an outward-pointing terminal velocity at γ(L)∈∂M₀, and an interior-supported f sampled along the arc; label I_{g₀}f(γ)=∫₀ᴸ f(γ(t))dt. Do not suggest all geodesics are maximal or that the diagram proves injectivity.
editorial_candidates.certainty: Editorial only; the source does not require a diagram and no mathematical defect is asserted.
